subject: Request: SOC 2 Type II scope & bridge letter for StratusGrid subservice (BlueHarbor Health)
messages:
From: Laura Chen <compliance@blueharborhealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@blueharborhealth.com, Samir Patel <samir.patel@clearpath-audit.com>
Date: 2028-05-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: SOC 2 scope and bridge letter request - StratusGrid subservice

Hi Karthik,

We're starting our vendor security assessment for Redwood as part of BlueHarbor Health's Q3 procurement for a pilot. Our external auditor (cc'd) has two items they need to close our risk review:

1) A copy of your most recent SOC 2 Type II report covering the period Jan 1, 2027 - Dec 31, 2027 (or equivalent attestation).
2) A bridge letter or management assertion that clarifies whether StratusGrid (the public cloud provider Redwood uses for a subset of services) is included in the scope of your SOC 2 report, or whether you treat it as a subservice organization/carve-out. If it's a carve-out, we need a mapping of responsibilities (what Redwood controls vs StratusGrid controls) and any evidence we can provide to our auditor to rely on the cloud provider's report.

Additional ask: list of subprocessors that touch PHI or ePHI, and whether any of those subprocessors have separate SOC/ISO attestations. If you have an inventory or an existing "subservice responsibility matrix," please attach.

Can you confirm the timeline for providing the SOC 2 report and a bridge letter or a proposed statement (we can accept a draft to share with our auditors)? Our auditor would like these items by EOD May 11 to keep our procurement timeline.

Thanks,
Laura Chen
Director, Vendor Risk Management
BlueHarbor Health

--

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Date: 2028-05-09T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 scope and bridge letter request - StratusGrid subservice

Hi Laura — thanks for the note and the clear asks. Looping in Marissa (security/compliance lead), Mina (cloud ops), and Ben (account lead) so we can get you what you need.

Short answers up front:
- We can provide a copy of our SOC 2 Type II report for the period Jan 1, 2027 — Dec 31, 2027.
- StratusGrid is treated as a subservice organization for certain managed storage and object lifecycle features used by Redwood; we rely on StratusGrid's SOC/assessments for those control areas. That said, Redwood performs full operational controls for encryption-in-use, key management (customer-managed KMS optional), access control, and application-layer logging.

We will: 
1) Attach a redacted SOC 2 report and a one-page SOC summary for your auditor.
2) Provide a bridge letter template stating the audited period and clarifying subservice scope (we can sign and return).
3) Share our subservice responsibility matrix that maps specific services and control ownership between Redwood and StratusGrid.
4) Provide a list of subprocessors that may handle PHI/ePHI with attestations where available.

Timeline: we'll aim to get a first pass over to you by EOD May 11 as requested. If Samir needs the cloud provider contact info for direct evidence requests, we can include StratusGrid's audit liaison in the bridge letter.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Manager, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Hi Laura / Samir —

Attached: redwood_soc2_type2_summary_2027.pdf, redwood_subservice_responsibility_matrix.xlsx, and a signed bridge letter (bridge_letter_template_redwood_signed.pdf). A few key clarifications included in the matrix:

- Audit period for Redwood's SOC 2 Type II: 2027-01-01 to 2027-12-31 (full trust services criteria for security and availability).
- StratusGrid services listed as subservice organizations in scope: StratusGrid Object Storage (for model artifacts), StratusGrid Ephemeral Compute (in certain shared-tenant pools), and StratusGrid Log Ingestion Service (for raw telemetry).
- Controls we rely on StratusGrid for: physical security, hypervisor isolation, and certain infrastructure patching attestations (as documented in StratusGrid's SOC/ISO reports).
- Redwood-owned controls: tenant encryption-at-rest using customer-derived keys (where customer opts-in), application-layer access control, token-level auditing, K/V cache handling, and response redaction routines.

Subprocessor list (high level):
- StratusGrid (cloud infra) — has SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001; contact: audit-liason@stratusgrid.example
- LogStream Inc (managed logging pipeline) — SOC 2 Type II
- KeySafe Ltd (optional KMS provider for some customers) — ISO 27001 only

We've redacted customer-identifying details from the SOC report per our policy but the bridge letter includes a point-of-contact if ClearPath needs to request additional evidence from StratusGrid. If your auditor wants direct access to StratusGrid evidence, we can coordinate an evidence handoff — please confirm who at ClearPath will initiate that.

Next steps:
1) Laura — please confirm receipt and let us know if you want Redwoods' compliance lead to introduce ClearPath to StratusGrid's audit team.
2) Samir — if you need any clarifications in the bridge language, we can make edits quickly; otherwise sign-off would be appreciated.

Thanks — happy to discuss on a quick call if helpful (we're available tomorrow morning).

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Manager, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
